requirements.description: A schema-stamped per-Profile lock admits one daemon owner, serializes stale takeover, recovers orphaned takeover state, releases only matching ownership, and fails loud on malformed or unsupported metadata.

The daemon registry owns one runtime per Session, shares concurrent creation, runs different Sessions independently when one is blocked in Provider work, reconciles incomplete durable lifecycle events without resuming work, and closes all runtimes before releasing the Profile lock.

The daemon serves strict protocol-v1 NDJSON only on the Profile-local Unix socket, verifies mode 0600, bounds frames and per-Client work, and dispatches the complete attach method surface after initialize.

Atomic subscription setup validates sinceSeq against the authoritative durable Session tail, accepts equality, rejects beyond-tail cursors as unsafe-sequence, and orders success before exact canonical replay and deferred live delivery with no second sequence authority; unsubscribe prevents later events and approval resolution is first-response-wins.
Client disconnect removes only its subscriptions without canceling Session work; reconnect replay remains contiguous, and a slow or overloaded Client is disconnected without blocking healthy Clients.

Per-Profile launchd and systemd user-service definitions use exact argv, restrictive permissions, schema-stamped ownership, fail-closed drift classification, and bounded lifecycle commands without mutating foreign definitions.

Foreground serve composes the filesystem kernel and attach socket with ordered cleanup; readiness requires a protocol initialize handshake, in-process auto-start callers share one readiness operation while the Profile lock enforces one cross-process owner, and doctor reports socket safety, daemon readiness, lock liveness/schema failures, and basic Provider-auth presence without exposing credential values.
